BEN HOROWITZ SAYS AMAZON $AMZN CEO ANDY JASSY TOLD HIM AI SUPPLY IS SOLD OUT BEYOND 2028

"I said, yeah, like we're out of everything till 2028. He's like, oh, it's beyond 2028."

Then he explained why that makes AI nothing like the dot-com bubble

"In the internet bubble, we didn't have enough demand because we had to build the internet. People had to get broadband. Originally they had to get their browser at Fry's. There weren't enough consumers on the internet to absorb all the bandwidth that had gotten built out."

"The lack of demand killed it. We don't really have a lack of demand in AI, so I think the dynamics will be different."

He did flag one risk. "If you get into a pathological debt situation, that can wreck anybody."

He said that's why Andreessen Horowitz isn't invested in any of the neoclouds. "That whole thing scares me, having been through it."

ON THIS DAY IN 1879, THOMAS EDISON CREATED THE FIRST PRACTICAL, LONG-LASTING LIGHT BULB

For months, his bulbs had burned out after just a few hours. His platinum filament kept melting.

The fix came while he was idly rolling a piece of carbon between his fingers. It gave him an idea: turn other materials into carbon and use them as the filament.

He tried a carbonized cotton thread inside a glass vacuum bulb, and it gave off a soft orange glow.

It burned for about 15 hours.

THE TESLA $TSLA SEMI IS NOW IN VOLUME PRODUCTION

The top version can go 500 miles fully loaded at 82,000 lbs, at an efficiency of 1.7 kWh per mile.

That means it uses about a third of the energy of a comparable diesel truck to haul the same load. In trucking, energy is one of the biggest costs per mile, so Tesla says that gives Semi operators a real advantage.

The Nevada factory is built for 25,000 Semis a year, and Tesla deployed its first pre-assembled Megacharger to support the ramp.

BREAKING: The NAHB Housing Market Index fell -3 points in October, to 29, its lowest level since June 2012.

This marks the 2nd consecutive monthly decline in homebuilder sentiment, totaling -6 points, marking the largest 2-month decrease since June 2025.

All 3 components deteriorated, with current sales falling -2 points, to 33, the lowest since June 2012.

Sales expectations dropped -5 points, to 32, the lowest since November 2022, while buyer traffic plunged -5 points, to 18, the lowest since April 2012, excluding the 2020 pandemic.

Furthermore, 43% of builders cut prices this month, the highest proportion of any month from 2020 to 2026.

The affordability crisis is putting further pressure on homebuilder sentiment.
